ai.title: Evals runner: add final flushStep() on finish event
ai.summary: CodebuffRunner now calls flushStep() when receiving a 'finish' event if responseText, toolCalls, or toolResults contain data. This ensures the final step's accumulated data is flushed before the runner completes, preventing potential loss of trailing output in evals. Change scoped to evals/git-evals/runners/codebuff.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant stops running a test in a hidden evaluation setup, it now makes sure to save any text or results it was still working on before fully shutting down. Previously, the last bit of output could be dropped if it arrived right as the test finished. This only affects the internal system that checks how the assistant is performing, so you won't see any difference unless you're running those behind-the-scenes tests.

eli5.text: The assistant can now generate a shorter summary of the files in a project's folder, about the length of a long text message, instead of always producing the full, detailed listing. This smaller summary is available when the assistant needs a lighter-weight view of the project, such as in a "lite" mode, and both the place that defines what the assistant can access and the place that fills in its instructions were updated to recognize this new option. If you inspected the setup yourself, you would see a new entry alongside the existing file-listing instructions, and the assistant's helper files now include a line that creates this condensed summary capped at roughly two thousand five hundred words. ai.summary: Spinner message changed from 'Reading through files...' to 'Processing results...' in npm-app/src/client.ts. This reflects the actual state during file processing. Internal UI text update only.

eli5.text: If you use the app and watch the loading message that appears while it works through your files, it now says 'Processing results...' instead of 'Reading through files...'. That's the only change you'd notice. It's already live, and it only updates the wording to better match what the app is actually doing at that moment.

ai.title: base-lite switches to gpt-5 medium effort with strict tool-use
ai.summary: base-lite agent definition updated to openai/gpt-5 with reasoningOptions effort 'medium' and exclude true. New base-quick.ts added using openai/gpt-5-chat lite. Prompting overhaul removes end_turn tool requirement, enforcing tool usage per response unless task complete. baseAgentSystemPrompt now accepts mode parameter ('lite'|'normal'|'max'|'experimental') to conditionally inject proactive execution guidance. File tree prompt token limit reduced from 20_000 to 10_000 in backend templates.

eli5.text: Today the lightweight assistant you can ask to brainstorm ideas switched to a smarter model that thinks a bit harder before answering, instead of the previous quick-thinking version. That assistant also lost a helper that used to let it stop itself mid-conversation, so from now on it will keep using tools until your request is fully done rather than pausing early. A new, even simpler assistant called quick was added for tasks that need a fast, no-frills response. You will notice this if you ask either assistant to do something multi-step, because they will work through it continuously instead of stopping after a single partial reply.

ai.title: Add CODEOFCONDUCT.md
ai.summary: Added CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md establishing community standards for Codebuff. Defines encouraged/restricted behaviors, reporting via support@codebuff.com, and scope. Adapted from Contributor Covenant 3.0. Repo root only.

eli5.text: Codebuff has published a new document at the top of its project that spells out how community members are expected to treat each other, what kinds of behavior are not allowed, and how to report concerns by emailing support@codebuff.com. The rules apply to all official community spaces and events, and they were adapted from a widely used public template. If you participate in Codebuff's community or contributor activities today, these are the standards you are now held to.

ai.title: Move fullResponseChunks log key after messages
ai.summary: Relocated `fullResponseChunks` in the logging object within `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`. This change ensures the chunks are logged after the message history and tool results. The modification is internal to the backend agent step execution logic. No user-facing behavior or API changes resulted from this reordering.

eli5.text: You wouldn't notice this change, it only moved a piece of diagnostic logging within the backend's agent-step execution so that a chunk-of-response field is now recorded after the message history and tool results instead of before them. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping in internal logging logic, with no effect on behavior, performance, or user-facing features.

ai.title: Web agent detail view renders definition as TypeScript
ai.summary: Web agent detail page replaces `JsonViewer` with new `TypeScriptViewer` component in `web/src/app/publishers/[id]/agents/[agentId]/[version]/page.tsx`. Agent definitions now render with syntax highlighting and field ordering via `prism-react-renderer` instead of raw JSON. New `web/src/components/agent/typescript-viewer.tsx` handles serialization, enforcing preferred key order for fields like `id`, `displayName`, `systemPrompt`, and `handleSteps`. Prompt strings and `handleSteps` functions receive special formatting to preserve readability.

eli5.text: When you open the detail page for a specific version of an agent, its technical definition now displays as neatly formatted, color-coded text instead of plain, unstyled JSON. Each important setting like the agent's name, instructions, and step-handling code appears with its own readable formatting, making the configuration easier to scan and understand. This affects anyone viewing agent definitions on the internal web publisher detail pages, and the improvement is already live.
